chapters.title: Kali Yuga — The Age of Darkness

verses.sanskrit: कलौ दशसहस्राणि हरिरेव कलौ युगे | पूज्यते च नमस्यश्च केशवो नान्यदैवतम् ||
verses.transliteration: kalau daśasahasrāṇi harireva kalau yuge | pūjyate ca namasyaśca keśavo nānyadaivatam ||
verses.translation: In Kali Yuga, for ten thousand years, Hari alone is worthy of worship and salutation — Keshava, and no other deity.
verses.hindi: कलियुग में दस हजार वर्षों तक केवल हरि (केशव) ही पूजनीय और नमस्करणीय हैं — किसी अन्य देवता की नहीं।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana's opening paradox: even in the worst age, the path to the divine remains open. Not through elaborate ritual or caste privilege — but through direct, simple devotion (bhakti) to Hari. The Kali Yuga, for all its darkness, democratises the spiritual path: complex Vedic rituals requiring priests, purity, and perfect conditions are replaced by the single, accessible requirement of sincere devotion.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मस्य ह्रासः कलौ काले सत्यस्य च परिक्षयः | शनैः शनैर्जगत्सर्वमधर्मे संप्रतिष्ठते ||
verses.transliteration: dharmasya hrāsaḥ kalau kāle satyasya ca parikṣayaḥ | śanaiḥ śanairjagatsarvamadharme saṃpratiṣṭhate ||
verses.translation: In the Kali Age, dharma declines and truth diminishes. Gradually, gradually, the whole world becomes established in adharma.
verses.hindi: कलियुग में धर्म का ह्रास और सत्य का क्षय होता है। धीरे-धीरे सारा जगत अधर्म में स्थापित हो जाता है।
verses.commentary: "Shanaiḥ shanaiḥ" — gradually, gradually. The Kalki Purana's most sobering insight about the fall of dharma: it does not happen suddenly. It is a slow erosion. Each small compromise normalises the next; each tolerated injustice makes the next injustice easier to tolerate. The world is not destroyed by one catastrophic decision but by a thousand small ones that are each individually rationalised.
verses.wordMeaning: "Shanaiḥ shanaiḥ" — gradually, gradually. The Kalki Purana's most sobering insight about the fall of dharma: it does not happen suddenly. It is a slow erosion. verses.sanskrit: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत | अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata | abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Whenever dharma declines, O Bharata, and whenever adharma rises — at that time I manifest myself.
verses.hindi: जब-जब धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म का उत्थान होता है — तब-तब मैं अपने आपको प्रकट करता हूँ।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana is the final, most extreme expression of the Gita's promise (4.7-8). Every prior avatar responded to a specific form of adharma; Kalki responds to the total collapse — the end of the cycle. But the principle is identical across all manifestations: the divine does not abandon the world. The response is proportional to the depth of the crisis. When the crisis reaches its absolute extreme, the response is absolute.

verses.sanskrit: शम्भले विष्णुयशसः गृहे प्रादुर्भविष्यति | सुमत्याः पुत्र रूपेण कल्किर्विष्णुयशाः सुतः ||
verses.transliteration: śambhale viṣṇuyaśasaḥ gṛhe prādurbhaviṣyati | sumatyāḥ putra rūpeṇa kalkir viṣṇuyaśāḥ sutaḥ ||
verses.translation: In Shambhala, Kalki will appear in the home of Vishnuyasha, born as the son of Sumati — the son of Vishnuyasha, Kalki.
verses.hindi: शम्भल में विष्णुयश के घर, सुमति के पुत्र रूप में कल्कि का प्रादुर्भाव होगा।
verses.commentary: The specificity of the Kalki Purana's prophecy is philosophically significant: the avatar appears in a particular village (Shambhala), in a particular family, through a particular mother. The divine does not descend abstractly — it arrives in concrete, specific form, through the most ordinary human channel (a mother and father, a home, a birth). Even the most cosmic intervention is local, particular, and human in its arrival.

chapters.title: The New Satya Yuga — Restoration of Dharma

verses.sanskrit: सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं सत्यमेव परो धर्मः | सत्यव्रतो भव नित्यं सत्यात् किञ्चिन्न विद्यते ||
verses.transliteration: satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ satyameva paro dharmaḥ | satyavrato bhava nityaṃ satyāt kiñcinna vidyate ||
verses.translation: Everything is established in truth. Truth alone is the supreme dharma. Always be devoted to truth — there is nothing higher than truth.
verses.hindi: सब कुछ सत्य में प्रतिष्ठित है। सत्य ही परम धर्म है। सदा सत्य-व्रती रहो — सत्य से ऊँचा कुछ नहीं है।
verses.commentary: The foundation of the new Satya Yuga is precisely what the Kali Yuga destroyed: satya — truth as lived practice, not just intellectual assent. The Kalki Purana distinguishes "satyavrata" (one who is vowed to truth) from one who merely knows truth. The new age begins not with external conditions changing but with individuals re-committing, internally, to telling the truth — to themselves first, then to others.

verses.sanskrit: पुनः प्रवर्तते धर्मो नृणां चारित्रसंयुतः | कृतं त्रेता द्वापरं च कलिश्चैव पुनः पुनः ||
verses.transliteration: punaḥ pravartate dharmo nṛṇāṃ cāritrasaṃyutaḥ | kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliścaiva punaḥ punaḥ ||
verses.translation: Dharma, accompanied by good character, turns again among humans. Krita (Satya), Treta, Dvapara, and Kali — again and again.
verses.hindi: मनुष्यों में सदाचार-सहित धर्म पुनः प्रवृत्त होता है। सतयुग, त्रेता, द्वापर और कलियुग — बार-बार।
verses.commentary: "Punaḥ punaḥ" — again and again. The Kalki Purana's final and most important teaching: the cycle is not linear. There is no permanent fall and no permanent golden age. Satya Yuga and Kali Yuga alternate eternally. This is not fatalism — it is liberation from both despair (things will never get better) and complacency (we have arrived at the permanent good). Every Satya Yuga will age into Kali; every Kali Yuga will be reborn as Satya. The work of dharma is therefore eternal, never final — and never hopeless.

verses.sanskrit: कलौ कृष्णावतारे तु यदा पापं समं महत् | तदा कल्की समुत्पन्नो धर्मं स्थापयते पुनः ||
verses.transliteration: kalau kṛṣṇāvatare tu yadā pāpaṃ samaṃ mahat | tadā kalkī samutpanno dharmaṃ sthāpayate punaḥ ||
verses.translation: In Kali Yuga, when evil becomes great, then Kalki is born to re-establish dharma.
verses.hindi: कलियुग में, जब पाप बहुत बढ़ जाता है, तब कल्कि जन्म लेते हैं धर्म की पुनः स्थापना के लिए।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana's core teaching on the tenth avatar. Kalki does not come when the world is comfortable — he comes when evil has reached its maximum extent. This is the divine homeostasis: the system self-corrects when the deviation becomes extreme. The birth of Kalki is not a reward for the world but an emergency response to its deepest crisis.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kalki Purana's core teaching on the tenth avatar. Kalki does not come when the world is comfortable — he comes when evil has reached its maximum extent. verses.sanskrit: कल्किर्देवो महाबाहुः श्वेताश्वो देवदत्तः | अभ्युत्थाय कलौ युगे धर्मं स्थापयते प्रिये ||
verses.transliteration: kalkirdevo mahābāhuḥ śvetāśvo devadattaḥ | abhyutthāya kalau yuge dharmaṃ sthāpayate priye ||
verses.translation: Kalki, the mighty-armed god, with white horse Devadatta, arises in Kali Yuga to establish dharma, O beloved.
verses.hindi: कल्कि देव, महाबाहु, श्वेत अश्व देवदत्त के साथ, कलियुग में उठकर धर्म की स्थापना करते हैं, हे प्रिये।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana describes the final avatar: Kalki, the mighty-armed god, riding the white horse Devadatta. He arises in Kali Yuga to establish dharma. This is the divine response to the nadir of the age — not passive observation but active intervention. The white horse symbolises purity and the sword symbolises the decisive cutting of adharma. Kalki is the assurance that dharma will always be restored.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kalki Purana describes the final avatar: Kalki, the mighty-armed god, riding the white horse Devadatta. He arises in Kali Yuga to establish dharma. verses.sanskrit: शम्भले ग्रामे जन्म कल्किस्य विष्णुरात्मजः | परशुरामशिक्षितः सर्वशास्त्रविद् विशारदः ||
verses.transliteration: śambhale grāme janma kalkisya viṣṇurātmajaḥ | paraśurāmaśikṣitaḥ sarvaśāstravid viśāradaḥ ||
verses.translation: Kalki, son of Vishnu, is born in Shambhala village, trained by Parashurama, learned in all scriptures, and wise.
verses.hindi: कल्कि, विष्णु के पुत्र, शम्भल ग्राम में जन्म लेते हैं, परशुराम द्वारा शिक्षित, सभी शास्त्रों में पारंगत और विशारद।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana details Kalki's birth and education: born in Shambhala village, trained by Parashurama (the warrior-sage avatar), learned in all scriptures, and wise. This establishes that the dharma-restorer is not born spontaneously but is prepared through training and education. The divine intervention is not magic but the culmination of preparation. Shambhala represents the hidden place of purity where the renewal begins.
verses.wordMeaning: The Kalki Purana details Kalki's birth and education: born in Shambhala village, trained by Parashurama (the warrior-sage avatar), learned in all scriptures, and wise. verses.sanskrit: धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः धर्मो हन्ति हतः क्रिया | धर्मो न प्रशश्यते किञ्चित् धर्मेण तप्यते अमृतम् ||
verses.transliteration: dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ dharmaḥ hanti hatāḥ kriyā | dharmaḥ na praśaśyate kiñcid dharmeṇa tapyate amṛtam ||
verses.translation: Dharma protects when protected; dharma destroys when destroyed. Dharma never perishes; through dharma, immortality is attained.
verses.hindi: धर्म रक्षा करता है जब रक्षित होता है; धर्म नष्ट करता है जब नष्ट किया जाता है। धर्म कभी नहीं मरता; धर्म से अमृत प्राप्त होता है।
verses.commentary: The Kalki Purana states the reciprocal nature of dharma: when you protect dharma, dharma protects you; when you destroy dharma, dharma destroys you. This is not a threat but a description of the structure of reality. Dharma is the principle of order; when you align with it, it sustains you; when you violate it, it undermines you. The verse concludes that dharma never perishes — it is eternal — and through dharma, immortality is attained.
